summary: The extension of Doble Play: after the initial Enchufla, the leader chains passes/checks past two followers ('first and second base') and picks up the third follower along the circle into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla with your starting follower on 1-3, then travel to the first follower on your right on 5-7 with a check/clap.
Continue to the second follower on 1-3 (or execute a quick Enchufla pass) and advance toward the third follower on 5-7.
Collect the third follower on 1-3 and finish with Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Execute the starting Enchufla on 1-3 and hold your perimeter station on 5-7 with a rhythmic basic.
Maintain the outer circle on 1-3 and 5-7, clapping or turning as passing leaders complete the first and second bases.
Connect with the third incoming leader on 1-3 and complete Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: Losing count of how many followers you have passed and stopping at the wrong station.
Cutting straight across the middle of the Rueda and causing a traffic jam.
variations: Shouting '¡Uno! ¡Dos! ¡Tres!' as the Rueda hits each base.

name: Un Tarro
summary: The 'Bull Horn': the quickest partner-change call in Rueda de Casino—starting from closed position (or Guapea), the leader steps directly backward/anticlockwise on 1-3 to hook the next follower without a Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Release your current follower on count 1 and step backward/anticlockwise along the circle on 1-2-3 to arrive directly in front of the next follower.
Connect immediately in closed hold (or Guapea) with the new follower on 5-6-7, continuing the basic step without a Dile Que No transition.

followerSteps.text: Continue your basic step in place along the circle on 1-2-3 while keeping your frame ready as your current leader steps back.
Connect seamlessly in closed hold (or Guapea) with the new leader arriving in front of you on 5-6-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Leaders stepping backward blindly on 1-2-3 without glancing over their shoulder to check spacing.
Trying to lead a Dile Que No on 5-7 when the Rueda is staying in closed 'Arriba' position.
Bumping elbows with the incoming follower.
variations: Un Tarro con Mentira (faking the step back on 1-3 and returning to the same partner on 5-7).

name: Vacílala con Bamboleo
summary: A musical, Timba-infused variation of Vacílala where the free turn opens into a low-grounded 'bamboleo' (swaying body isolation / Despelote groove) before reconnecting for Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a clean Vacílala free turn for the follower on 1-3 while stepping around the circular arc.
Instead of immediately picking up the follower in closed hold, face the follower in open Suelta on 5-6-7 and sink into a grounded 'bamboleo' (lateral ribcage/hip sway and shoulder groove).
Continue the playful Bamboleo interaction on 9-11, then reconnect smoothly on 12 to lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the traveling clockwise Vacílala turn on 1-2-3, spotting the leader on 3.
Catch the visual cue from the leader and drop into a fluid 'bamboleo' sway (thoracic isolation and Cuban hip pendulum) on 5-6-7.
Finish the solo body-movement groove on 9-11, offer your frame on 12, and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Grabbing the follower on count 5 when she is mid-groove.
Doing the Bamboleo sway with stiff knees or losing the underlying clave timing.
Forgetting to re-establish visual and physical connection by count 12 for Dile Que No.
variations: Extending the Bamboleo groove for an extra eight-count during a Bamboleo or Havana D'Primera bomba/mambo breakdown.

name: Vacílala con Columbia
summary: An explosive Afro-Cuban fusion figure where the Vacílala turn breaks open into a fast, athletic Rumba Columbia footwork challenge before reconnecting into Casino.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a crisp Vacílala free turn on 1-3, opening the space between you and the follower.
Drop into an athletic Rumba Columbia stance on 5-6-7, executing fast syncopated heel-toe/cross footwork and sharp shoulder/arm accents.
Resolve the Columbia shine on 9-11, re-establish open frame connection on 12, and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Complete the traveling Vacílala turn on 1-2-3 and face the leader.
Answer the leader's Columbia challenge with sharp solo footwork, rhythmic skirt work, or Changó/Ochún-inspired arm styling on 5-6-7.
Finish the solo exchange on 9-11 and step cleanly into Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Kicking or lunging too wide in the Columbia footwork on a crowded social dance floor.
Losing the 1-2-3, 5-6-7 Casino count when switching into 6/8 or syncopated Columbia rhythms.
Abruptly yanking the follower back into partnerwork on count 13.
variations: Incorporating a subtle vacunao / defense play on count 11 before Dile Que No.

name: Vacílala y Florea
summary: A stylish, expressive Vacílala variation where both partners embellish ('florean') the open turn with circular Paseo walks, Rumba Guaguancó play, and hand/arm flourishes before reconnecting.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a smooth Vacílala on 1-3, releasing connection to let the follower travel freely.
Circle the follower on 5-6-7 while 'floreando'—adding theatrical Cuban arm framing, cape-like passes, or playful Guaguancó decoys without touching.
Complete the circular orbit on 9-11, present a clear open frame on 12, and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Vacílala turn on 1-2-3 with controlled spotting.
'Florea' (blossom/embellish) on 5-6-7 with sweeping arm styling, skirt work, and circular walks while maintaining eye contact with the leader.
Glide into the pickup frame on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Turning your back on your partner and ignoring them during the 'floreo' section.
Drifting too far apart so you cannot reach each other cleanly by count 12.
Rushing the arm styling instead of breathing with the music.
variations: Leader drops to one knee or executes a slow body wave while the follower circles.

name: Vacílense
summary: The mutual version of Vacílala: both leader and follower execute simultaneous free turns while traveling around their shared circular orbit before reconnecting in Dile Que No or Guapea.

leaderSteps.text: From open Guapea on 1, give a clear inward rotational prep with the left-to-right connection, release on 2, and execute your own clockwise (right) free turn along the circle on 2-3.
Continue traveling forward around the circle on 5-6-7 to pick up the follower in closed or open frame for Dile Que No.

followerSteps.text: Feel the Vacílala prep on 1, release hands, and execute a smooth right (clockwise) traveling turn along the circle on 1-2-3.
Complete the circular walk on 5-6-7, spotting the leader early to reconnect smoothly on count 7.

commonMistakes: Spinning frantically on the spot instead of traveling along the perimeter of the circle on 1-2-3.
Throwing the partner's arm on count 1, which pulls both dancers off balance.
Failing to spot each other on count 3, leading to a clumsy reconnection on 5-7.
variations: Adding a solo clap, shoulder shimmy, or Rumba accent on counts 4-5 before reconnecting.

name: Vamos Abajo / Vamos Arriba
summary: The directional marching calls in closed Rueda position: on 'Vamos Abajo' the leaders walk backward (followers forward) anticlockwise around the ring; on 'Vamos Arriba' the direction reverses so leaders walk forward clockwise.

leaderSteps.text: In closed hold for Vamos Abajo: step left foot back-and-side on 1-2-3 and right foot back on 5-6-7, traveling anticlockwise around the circle while guiding the follower forward.
When 'Vamos Arriba' (or 'Arriba') is called: check direction cleanly on 1-3 and walk forward clockwise around the circle on 5-7 while guiding the follower backward.

followerSteps.text: In closed hold for Vamos Abajo: walk forward anticlockwise around the circle on right (1-2-3) and left (5-6-7), keeping your chest connected to the leader's frame.
When 'Vamos Arriba' is called: feel the leader's chest check on 1-3 and walk backward clockwise around the circle on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Leaders taking huge backward steps during Vamos Abajo and stepping on the couple behind them.
Reversing direction abruptly on the wrong foot instead of using the 1-2-3 rock check.
Breaking closed hold into Guapea without a 'Dile Que No' call.
variations: Adding 'Me La Llevo' (continuous fast walking around the circle).
